dimension_grades.evidence: Project Alpha and the Blockers & Risks section are written as narrative prose paragraphs, not bullet points.
The Beta section has properly concise bullets, but the Alpha and Blockers sections are paragraphs, so not all status information meets this standard.
'Resolve the database migration issue' and 'Figure out coverage for Jake's absence' appear in both Blockers & Risks and Next Steps.

Next Steps contains 7 bullets including items like 'Update the project tracker' and 'Schedule sync with Platform team' that could be folded into project-level sections or omitted from a leadership update.
The email opens with 'Hope you had a good weekend! I wanted to give you a rundown...' — pleasantries and context-setting, not a status summary.
There is no single summary sentence capturing wins and timeline shifts; the database blocker and Jake's absence are buried in the body.
No line in the email explicitly signals whether the reader needs to act or not; the closing only says 'let me know if you have any questions.'
There is no summary line at all, so no label (plain or otherwise) is present.
The draft uses 'pretty significant setback,' 'real problem,' and 'scrambling' to describe the database migration issue — all alarm-register words.
'Could potentially push things back' is vague with no concrete estimate such as '~1 week.'
The draft says 'Will keep you posted as we learn more' with no specific date by which the resolution path will be clear.
The draft never states that the database issue or staffing gap does not require director intervention; it leaves escalation ambiguous.
The draft contains no internet-style abbreviations or casual shorthand labels such as 'TL;DR.'
The closing uses 'Best regards' which is overly formal, and the opening weekend pleasantry adds filler rather than approachable directness.

The update is written as a long narrative walkthrough ('I think it's worth walking through the details so you have full context') with no apparent awareness that Maria reads on mobile between meetings and needs brevity.
